t: A Tuscan commune that grew rich on wool cloth and banking and ruled most of Tuscany by the fifteenth century.
Its gold florin, minted from 1252, became a standard coin of international trade across Europe.
From 1434 the Medici steered the republic informally, and it was the birthplace of the Renaissance.
dyk: Florentine offices were filled by lot: names of eligible citizens were drawn from leather bags, and priors served for only two months.
ev: Death of Matilda of Canossa; Florentine citizens take control of their city
The Ordinances of Justice exclude the magnates from government
The Black Death kills perhaps half the population
Florence conquers Pisa after a long siege
Cosimo de’ Medici returns from exile and leads the republic
The Medici are expelled after the French invasion
Alessandro de’ Medici becomes Duke and the republic ends

f.founder: Citizens of the commune (consuls recorded from 1138)
